**3. What a pad is solid for** (`PadPurpose`: `press_fit`, `terminal`, `heat`, `stitching`; BOARD.md has the
table). Stored on the placed pad (`PadJoin::purpose`), the pad or the footprint (`Overrides::purpose`), an
enum, absent when unset, so boards and libraries without it are written as before. `zone.pad --purpose` and
`footprint.set --purpose` set it and, unless a connection is given or set, `solid` with it. A press-fit pin and
a stitching pad are not soldered (`PadClass::Bare`), a heat pad is a heat pad, a terminal is the solder pad
it is and solid by its purpose; `drc.solid_pad` is quiet for all four, `zone.thermals` lists them (`meant`,
the purpose), and `zone.relieve` keeps their setting where it removes a `solid` that says nothing. The default
did not move: a through-hole pin or an SMD pad in a pour is relieved.
*KiCad.* The published file format ("S-Expression Format", footprint pad, read 2026-11-22) has a `property`
token on pads with six values: BGA, global and local fiducial, test point, heat sink, castellated. One says
what a pad is in a pour: `pad_prop_heatsink` is read as `purpose: heat` and written back. It has no value for
a press-fit pin (D112 had left that to be looked up), a terminal or stitching: those are written as the
pad's `zone_connect` and listed by `export.pad_purpose`, and come back as solid pads without a purpose. No
KiCad source was read. The generated exposed pads and tabs keep their `zone_connection: solid` and get no
`purpose`: they are classed as heat pads by their paste windows and size already, and a property on them
would move every golden file of a generated footprint for nothing.
**4. Relief required.** `board.rules --thermal-required true` (`Rules::thermal_required`, stored with the
board, false by default, in no preset and no fab profile): the thermal findings of the fab check
(`fab.solid_pad`, `fab.thermal_nominal`, `fab.starved_thermal`, `fab.thermal_size`) are errors, so
`fab.export` refuses (`fab.check_failed`, nothing written; `force` exports all the same, as it does past
any error of the fab check), and no waiver takes an error away. A pad is let through by what item 3 says: a purpose,
or a placed pad's own setting with its reason, which is also what the repair writes for the pads it keeps
solid. A bare `solid` on a pad or footprint is then not taken as meant. `drc.run`'s own findings stay
warnings. *The default stays as it was*, warnings: the user was asked which they want and has not said, and
an error by default refuses the export of every imported board (664 solder pads solid on the corpus as its
projects make it, D109). *(D120: the user has said; required by
default.)*
**5. Copper on the two pads of a chip part, against each other: not written.** A warning for a two-pad part
with very unequal copper on its pads needs a number for "very". Read for one, 2026-11-22: Eurocircuits, "PCB
assembly guidelines: tombstoning" ("the difference in thermal mass between pads of the same component", "the
aim is to make the track width to each pad of the component the same width", "at least 0.25 mm of track before
it connects to the copper area"); Nordson EFD, "Tombstone troubleshooting"; the DFM pages of JLCPCB, Cadence,
Autodesk and Altium on tombstoning. All say the two pads should have the same copper; none gives a ratio or a
percentage, and IPC-7351's text was not found in what could be read. So no threshold was invented and no rule
added. What there is: `drc.solid_pad` names the risk when one pad of a two-pad part is solid and the other is
not (D109), and Eurocircuits' 0.25 mm of track before a copper area is a number a later rule could stand on.
**Golden files and tests.** One golden file moved and was blessed again on purpose,
`tests/golden/exchange/tiny-ipc2581.xml`: the round pad of the tiny board whose spoke is trimmed has it with
the corners of the trim rounded (four points for two in the plane's outline), and two cutouts in that plane
that were a few nanometers wide (3.5429 to 3.6045 mm by 0.000002 mm: the seam between a trimmed spoke and
the pour's rounded edge) are gone. No other golden file and no snapshot moved: the tests of zones, thermal
relief, DRC, fab check, KiCad import and export, the exchange formats, the model's round trip, the CLI and
MCP snapshots, the Gerber cross-check, the board render and the demo board were run. New tests:
`tests/zone_relieve.rs` (above); in `tests/thermal_relief.rs` the repair against the repair from scratch,
`solid_for_a_purpose`, `thermal_relief_required`, `relieve_joins_a_pad_nothing_joined`, and the blockers in
`starved_thermal`; in `board::thermal` `purposes`, `a_track_around_the_corner` and the copper count in
`solid_and_starved`; in `board::zones` `trimmed_spoke_is_no_narrower_than_a_track` and the allowed area kept
in `reliefs_reused_give_the_fill_made_from_scratch`.
**KiCad.** In CI, on the branch `ci/thermal-3`, KiCad 10 (the oracle and corpus jobs; `gh workflow run CI`):
- commit 56377fc (the first form of the trimming rule): `Oracle tests` and `Open-source corpus` passed, as
  did `Test & lint` on Linux and macOS (the whole suite); the run was cancelled there.
- commit cd7e4bc (the rule as it stands): `Oracle tests` failed in the Gerber cross-check alone: on the
  features board the fourth spoke of J1.1, the pin at the board edge, is now the one on the diagonal beside
  the edge, trimmed to what the edge clearance leaves (0.063 mm² on `B.Cu` at x 9.69 to 10.07, y 1.06 to
  1.37 mm), where D112's was the whole one across the pad: of the directions that fit, the one that spreads
  best is taken, and more fit now. KiCad drops that spoke as it dropped D112's. The entry of `KNOWN` was
  moved and says so. `kicad_agrees_on_starved_thermals` passed: `starved3` reported by both, `starved2` by
  neither, and on `turned3` no finding on the exported fill (KiCad counts the diagonals cadlab places) and
  "zone min spoke count 2; actual 1" on KiCad's own refill, as in D112.
- commit 7d28cf8 (the same code, `KNOWN` moved): `Oracle tests` and `Open-source corpus` passed (KiCad
  10.0.8): all twelve projects `ok`, no finding without an allowance on either side. On the corpus the two
  tools still count on their own fills (the allowances of D109, on both sides): cadlab reports 68 pads as
  routed on five boards (39, 14, 11, 3 and 1), KiCad its own on its refills. `Test & lint` (the whole
  suite, fmt, clippy, rustdoc) passed on Linux, macOS and Windows, as did the freerouting, exchange and
  openEMS oracles, MSRV 1.95, cargo-deny and the benchmarks. The run was cancelled with the router on the
  corpus at a fixed work budget (informative), ems beside openEMS and freerouting on the corpus still
  going; the branch is deleted.
**Tried and dropped.**
1. *The repair read place by place*: each change measured on a fill of the places around it alone
   (`fill_zones_within`: the zones cut to windows around the changed pads and the pads beside them), the whole
   board filled once at the end and compared, the slow way taken when the two disagree. Built and measured on
   glasgow-revD1: the footprints' narrower spokes change 241 placed pads and the reliefs at the minimums 99,
   and with the margins a change can reach (a relief, twice the minimum width, a clearance) their windows
   took in 2541 and 2473 of the board's 2557 pads: a fill of the places was a fill of the board. And a fill
   cut to a window is the same region and not the same polygons, so the result was the reference's only as
   long as no decision sat on an arc's last micrometer. Taken out.
2. *Two fills kept per zone layer and the allowed area by a key of its own*: over the bound on cynthion at
   every fill (above).
3. *The repair working on necks by their copper*: a pad on one wide piece was then not tried with a narrower
   relief, and three pads of cynthion ended without effective relief. The repair works on the pieces as
   before; the rule counts by copper.
4. *A trimmed spoke dropped when narrower than a track, and D51's half-width test kept beside it*: the first
   form of the rule. On the corpus as routed it only took spokes away (nine more pads on one neck after the
   repair, 63 short by pieces for 55), and the U of D112's own test, with legs as long as it is wide, went
   back to one spoke: what D51 cut to the gap and the pour was pinched where the pour's rounded edge meets
   the gap, however wide the way. The rule as it stands (trimmed to the minimum track, within the allowed
   area) keeps that U's diagonals and 95 pads short as routed for 116.
**What got worse.** cynthion's pads short of two spokes (above: 23 to 31 by pieces, pads that were solid
before). Fills are not those of D117 where a spoke is trimmed: fewer where what was left was thinner than a
track, more where it was thinner than half the spoke and still a track, and a trimmed spoke is no longer cut
to the pad's gap and the pour, so it can run through allowed copper that the pour's minimum width removed
(it is a track's width of copper there, and keeps every clearance: it lies in the allowed area). Of the
other directions that fit, the one that spreads best is still the one taken, and a trimmed one can now be
taken where a whole one stood before (J1.1 of the features board, under **KiCad**): thinner copper, better
spread; a whole spoke was not given the preference. A pad whose
spokes at the minimum track width still cover two thirds of its outline is left as `drc.thermal_nominal`
after the repair on boards the routers made: the repair narrows spokes and does not take one away.
`LayerMemo` and `JointMemo` hold up to ten and two million points more in a process that fills (160 and 32 MB
at the bound). A fill of a board from nothing takes the building of the keys more (not measured apart). The
diagnostic's "its footprint leaves room for N" (`Joint::possible`, the zone's clearance around the boxes of
the footprint's pads) and what `blockers` finds in the way (the clearances the fill keeps, round the pads'
shapes) are two tests: on two balls of cynthion's `IC1` the first says two directions are free and the second
finds the footprint's own pads in all of them.
*Not done:* a router that moves a track off a pad's spoke on being told (`thermal::blockers` names them;
BOARD.md, "What a router must be told", says what the guide adapter would pass); fewer spokes for a pad that
four of them cover; the refill of a changed zone layer in less than its whole-layer booleans; `purpose` on
generated footprints; the 3D view.

### D120. Thermal relief is required by default: a board with a solder pad left solid in a pour does not leave through `fab.export` unless its rules say it may (2026-11-22)
D119 added the rule `thermal_required` and left it off, the user not having said which default they want. The
user decided on 2026-11-22: **on**. The reason is a board, not a principle: a forgotten relief made a large
board painful to solder, every ground pin of it a pad that the pour kept cold, and nothing between the layout
and the order had stopped it. A warning among the others of an export did not. An error that refuses the
export does.
**What is on.** `Rules::thermal_required` is true for a new board (`Rules::default`), in every built-in rule
preset (`ipc2`, `ipc3`: `rule-presets/ipc.toml` holds only what differs from the default and does not name the
rule; applying a preset starts from the default rules, so it switches the rule on again as it resets every other
rule, and `--preset ipc3 --thermal-required false` keeps it off; `--fab` derives lengths and leaves the rule as
the board has it), and for an imported KiCad board (KiCad
has no such rule; the import keeps the board's own, `kicad_import::rules::apply`). With it the four thermal
findings of the fab check (`fab.solid_pad`, `fab.thermal_nominal`, `fab.starved_thermal`, `fab.thermal_size`)
are errors, `fab.check` fails and `fab.export` refuses with `fab.check_failed`, nothing written, as D119
describes; `drc.run`'s own findings stay warnings.
**What an old file reads as: on.** The field was added after v0.0.5 and has been in no release, so no
released cadlab wrote it; every project saved before D119, and every one saved since without the switch, has
no such field. The native format's rules (DATA_MODEL.md: `schema_version`, migrations on load) say nothing
against giving an absent optional field its default, which is how every optional rule was added (ELECTRICAL.md:
"optional fields: projects without them load and save unchanged, so no schema migration was needed"); the
schema version stays 1 and there is no migration. The serialization turns over with the default: `true` is
left out, **`"thermal_required": false` is the only value saved**, so a board that was switched off stays off
and says so in its file, and a board saved with D119's `true` (between D119 and this, unreleased) reads as
before and loses the now redundant field at its next save. The price, taken knowingly: an existing project
whose pours hold solid solder pads is refused at its next export where it was exported with warnings before.
That is the forgotten relief the user wants caught, and the refusal names the ways out.
**The ways out**, all three in the hint of each finding and of the refusal (`fab::check::THERMAL_REQUIRED_HINT`;
the refusal counts the thermal errors among the fab check's):
1. `zone.relieve`: the repair, for pads in a pour.
2. The pad says what it is solid for: `zone.pad <ref.pad> --purpose press_fit|terminal|heat|stitching`,
   `footprint.set <footprint> --pads N --purpose ..`, or a placed pad's own setting with its reason
   (`zone.pad J1.3 --connection solid --reason "carries 12 A"`).
3. `board.rules --thermal-required false`: warnings again for this board, stored with it; `board.rules` then
   says in its text that relief is not required. `fab.export --force` exports past any error of the fab
   check, as before.
**What else changed with it.**
- *A pad solid by tracks.* `drc.solid_pad` has a second form, a pad with tracks wider than itself or copper
  drawings on two thirds of its outline and no pour (`Solid::Copper`). `zone.relieve` does not repair it (it
  works on pours), its hint offered a waiver, which takes no error away, and a pad's own `solid` setting did
  not count for it (`Joint::meant` looked at the connection a zone gives the pad, and there is no zone). Left
  so, the default would have refused a board with no way out but a purpose that does not fit or the switch.
  Now a pad's own setting counts where no zone holds the pad (`Joint::own_solid`; with the rule on, the placed
  pad's with its reason, as in a pour), and the hint under the rule names `zone.pad <pad> --purpose ..` and
  `--connection solid --reason ..` instead of the waiver. With the rule off a bare setting on such a pad
  is "meant" too, as it is in a pour.
- *The hint of the pour form* already named `zone.relieve` and `--purpose`; every thermal error now ends with
  the same sentence naming the three ways.
**Tests that changed, and what they mean now.**
- `tests/thermal_relief.rs`: `thermal_relief_required` starts from the default (errors, the export refused,
  the three ways in both hints), switches the rule off (warnings, a bare footprint setting meant; `false` in
  the command's output), and on again (`true` is not written). `solid_on_purpose_is_quiet` is the test of a
  board that does not require relief (bare setting meant, a waiver quiets the fab check) and now says so by
  switching the rule off first. `wide_track_into_a_pad` adds the track form under the rule: an error, not
  taken away by `zone.relieve` or a bare setting, taken away by the setting with its reason.
- `tests/drc_crosscheck.rs`, `cases_have_no_thermal_findings`: the case `local_settings` sets a header pin
  solid on its footprint (to compare a pad's `zone_connect` with KiCad) and says nothing of what for; under
  the rule that bare setting is not meant, and the test now expects exactly that one `drc.solid_pad` on J1.1
  there, none on any other case. Giving the pad `purpose: terminal` was tried and dropped: KiCad's format has
  no pad property for a terminal (D119), so the round trip lost it and `tests/kicad_pcb_import.rs` saw a
  changed footprint and one more finding after the import.
- `tests/agent_session6.rs`: the router enters the SoC's VSS pin U1.45 (a 0.2 mm QFN pin beside the exposed
  pad) with tracks wider than the pin, 78 % of its outline. The export is refused (asserted, with the hint and
  nothing written), and the replay sets the pins `zone.thermals` lists as solid, which must all be GND pins of
  U1, solid with a reason, then exports as before.
- Unit tests: `model::board::tests::thermal_relief_is_required_unless_said_otherwise` (default, presets, a
  board and rules without the field, only `false` written), `kicad_import::rules::tests::minimum_spokes`
  (an imported board requires relief).
- No golden file and no snapshot moved: `true` is not written, the default flow of every committed board has
  no pad the rule stops (the demo board has no pour), and no committed project carried the field.
- With the corpus (`CADLAB_CORPUS_DIR`): the only replay that exports an imported board is
  `agent_session4`'s ring light, and its two exports pass with the rule on (run here without `kicad-cli`).
**The documented flow.** A board with pours is exported after `zone fill`, `zone relieve`, `drc`: BOARD.md
("Relief required"), MANUFACTURING.md (fab profiles, `fab.export`), INTERFACES.md (the example session). The
demo board's five lines stand: it has no pour.
**What this costs, said plainly.** An imported board whose designer meant its pads solid (664 solder pads on
the corpus as its projects make it, D109) is refused until `zone.relieve` has run, its pads say what they are
solid for, or the rule is switched off; the import says the count and names the repair, as before. A board the
routers made can be refused for a fine-pitch pin entered by a track wider than itself (session 6), which no
repair fixes yet: the pad says it is meant, or the router is taught to neck down there (not done). *(D121: the
routers' tracks are laid no wider than the pad where they meet it.)* The fab
check's thermal errors cannot be waived, by D119.

### D121. guide 0.0.23 adopted: a negotiation that does not end begun again on finer grids, a via to the plane at the native router's price, a track no wider than the pad it meets from either router, a track moved off a pad's spoke; the default unchanged (2026-11-22)
The direction for this round, given on 2026-11-22: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on
every measure on every board, by porting into guide what the native router still does better. It does not end there.
This decision says what was ported, what that moved, and where guide is still behind, by board and measure. `guide =
{ version = "0.0.23", default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock` moves. Measured
with the crate from crates.io.
**1. A track enters a pad no wider than the pad** (D120's open point). Both routers entered a 0.2 mm pin with the
net's 0.22 to 0.3 mm track; the pad is then solid by its track, `fab.solid_pad` is an error since D120, and
`zone.relieve` repairs pours, not tracks. Counted first, at one fixed routing per board and router (`route_bench`
with a budget of 20 million nodes, the pass on and off; `Joint::wide`, pads met by a track wider than themselves,
copper drawings left out): guide's result had 91 such pads on corne-cherry, 58 on tinytapeout-demo (one of them
solid), 11 on glasgow-revD1 and 1 on buspirate5-rev10; the native router's 3, 3, 7 and 1.
- *guide 0.0.23 has the function* (`pcb::neck_at_pads`, with `pcb::PadEntry` and `pcb::pad_entries`): tracks that
  are routed, and pads with the widest a track may be at each; every part of a straight track whose middle line is
  nearer to a narrower pad of its net than half the track's width and a margin is cut out and laid at the pad's
  width along the same line. A function on a result, not a step of a run: the adapter hands routes back between its
  runs, and those stay of one width.

  tracks' nets by the shape of each layer, each with its shorter side as the check measures it (`zones::short_side`)
  to the micrometre under it and never under `min_track_width`; a margin of 25 µm (the 10 µm band of
  `thermal::joints`, as much again for the outward tolerances of the band and of a track's polygon, and 5 µm: with
  15 µm the pads still read as met by the wide part). `neck: false` leaves every track at its net's width, as the
  option says of the native router's own necking.

  either router; what is left under "wider" is copper drawings (the jumpers of tinytapeout-demo and lumenpnp-mobo,
  glasgow-revD1's net tie). 0 DRC errors, the same connections, vias and length. In the runs of the table below: no
  pad of any board is solid by copper that is no pour, with either router, in the 96 runs; the pads met by copper
  wider than themselves are tinytapeout-demo's 9, lumenpnp-mobo's 1 and glasgow-revD1's 1 in every run of both, all

points shared from the tenth round on in every order, the nets of the USB receptacle and the supplies (measured,
round by round). The native router has the same board in its comments for the same thing (`finer_grid`: "negotiation
then never settles (nrfmicro: 20 to 40 points still shared when it stops at 0.2 mm)") and runs again at the pitch
over 1.5, 2 and 3, then with another seed; its 0 open in D118's table came from a run at 0.133 mm. guide 0.0.23 does
that inside its negotiation: one at the first pitch that ended on its own with no more than a hundred points shared
is begun again at two thirds, a half and a third of the pitch, in the order given and in two others, the first that
ends with nothing shared kept; the price rises to a thousand there. Measured through the adapter at 60 s, one

### D122. guide 0.0.24 adopted: a via of a net with a pour at the native router's price on two layers, the way with less outside the pads, the runs that move routes ended where one has said it all, the first needless step whatever the time; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on every
board. It does not end there in this round either. This decision says what the two routers' results look like
stage by stage, what was ported from that, what it moved, and what is still behind, by board and measure and by
the nets that both routers complete. `guide = { version = "0.0.24", default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`;
nothing else in `Cargo.lock` moves. Measured with the crate from crates.io.
**The two routers stage by stage** (measured, with prints in both that are in neither release; one run of each
at 60 s on three threads unless said):
- *tinytapeout-demo, the native router*: its negotiation ends after 38 rounds and 17 s with 2 points shared,
  255 vias and 4686 mm; the nets taken out and routed again, 251 and 4615; after its rounds for the pours, 287
  and 4899; its pass for fewer vias takes 1.9 s and leaves 248 and 5013; its pull-tight, corner and gridless
  passes 244 and 4947. So its pass for fewer vias is worth 14 % of its vias for 2 % more track, the passes
  after it 1.3 % of the track, and it has 19 connections open in that run.
- *tinytapeout-demo, guide*: its negotiation at twice the pitch has 177 rounds in 23 s, with 3210 points shared
  after the first, 101 after the eleventh, and 12 to 116 in every round after that until its share ends; it
  ends with 458 vias and 5792 mm. Its pass for fewer vias takes 0.4 s and leaves 381 and 5660. The passes and
  the settling that close what is open leave 412 and 5978; cleanup has 1.8 s before the first run's deadline
  and leaves 393 and 5879; the later runs, what the fill makes needless and the ends inside the pads leave 344
  and 5453, with none open. So guide leaves its negotiation with half as many vias again as the native router
  leaves its own, and a fifth more track, and nothing after it takes that back: the gap is made in the rounds,
  not in what follows them. A pass for fewer vias that a faster search made complete would be worth what
  cleanup's is where it has the time (522 to 446 in 12.5 s, measured in a run whose negotiation was cut), and
  the native router's are 244.
- *At the native router's pitch* (guide's negotiation forced to the first pitch on this board of four layers,
  one run): a round takes 0.8 to 1.8 s where it took 0.15 s, the share ends it after its twelfth with 151 points
  shared (the native router: 18 after its twelfth), and the minute ends with 8 open for none, 399 vias and
  5418 mm. Not kept; D115 had the same of glasgow-revD1.
- *corne-cherry, the rounds of both* (two layers, the same pitch): 4792, 2220, 1457, 1020, 712, 471, 325, 280,
  237, 193, 141, 60, 34 and 18 points shared after the native router's first fourteen rounds, 10 to 28 for the
  nineteen after, and its negotiation ends after 9 s; 4338, 1942, 1373, 866, 638, 413, 370, 310, 289, 172, 160,
  157, 174 and 125 after guide's, 66 to 168 for the seventy after, 16 to 66 in its last twenty, and its share
  ends it after 19.7 s. They part at the tenth round: the native router's price for a shared point goes on
  rising (41, 66, 105, 169 steps) and guide's stops at thirty. That it stops is D115's, for the copper
  (corne-cherry at a thousand: 566 vias and 8269 mm for 506 and 7590), and D121 tried it rising again and did
  not keep it; it is what guide's time on this board is.
- *By net* (D121's dumps, one run of each): the nets that both complete with no via in either are as long or
  shorter with guide on every board (tinytapeout-demo -8 %, glasgow-revD1 -1.5 %); those with as many vias in
  both are 5 % longer with guide on the boards at twice the pitch (glasgow-revC3 +5.3 %, glasgow-revD1 +5.1 %,
  cynthion +5.5 %) and level at the first (corne-cherry -0.9 %); and the nets where guide has more vias are
  where its track is: tinytapeout-demo 43 nets with 144 vias for 66 and 2223 mm for 1965 (+13 %), glasgow-revD1
  78 nets with 337 for 208 and +14 %, corne-cherry 29 nets with 189 for 111 and +20 %. The nets where guide
  has fewer vias are shorter with it or level, but on glasgow-revC3 (+8 %). A net that went under another in
  an early round and stayed there is longer and has the vias (D115: "its negotiation's vias only rise").
- *The nets with zones and the others* (D121's runs, four of each): the vias that guide has over the native
  router are those of the nets with zones on corne-cherry (140 to 157 against 65 to 71; the others 349 to 368
  against 370 to 416), half of them on buspirate5-rev10 (86 to 112 against 74 to 92; 226 to 237 against 214 to
  230) and a third on tinytapeout-demo (79 to 86 against 41 to 68; 268 to 292 against 203 to 223), and on the
  two small boards all of them: lumenpnp-ringlight's ground has 2 for 1, and buspirate-flash-sop's GND_CHIP 2
  with no track for none, vias that join the pieces of its pour on the two sides, made by the run on the
  filled board and by the run for shorter ways.
**What was ported.**
1. *A via of a net with a pour at the native router's price for it, on two layers* (guide 0.0.24). The native
   router's pass for fewer vias routes a net again with a via at forty steps and keeps what is at most a tenth
   longer; a ground of seventy pads comes out of it with a track from pad to pad where a via stood. guide's
   pass has the same price and the same rule and takes none of them (measured: given the time to end, with
   the nets with planes first, corne-cherry's grounds have 131 to 157 vias over three orders for 130 to 157).
   So the price is the negotiation's from its first round, for a net with a pour at the first pitch, and
   eight times the passes' price in the stubs that take a pad back to its fill on a board of two layers. At
   twice the pitch, where the planes are inside the board and a via is the way to them, D121's five steps
   stay. Tried at twenty and thirty steps: 464 and 484 vias with 1 and 4 open, 457 and 459 with 5 and none,
   over two orders.
2. *Of two ways as long as each other, the one with less outside the pads* (guide 0.0.24, in the cleanup that
   pulls a run tight). The native router ends a route on the first cell that is on its pad's copper; guide
   goes to the pad's middle, and of the two octilinear ways there took the first that was legal.
   buspirate-rs232's nets of two pads between its SOICs and their capacitors: 2.6 mm each for the native
   router's 1.8 mm, 2.1 mm now.
3. *The runs that move routes ended where one has said all there is* (the adapter). cynthion's eight nets at
   its net ties have no way with any route moved; D117 ended such runs after two that gain nothing. One is
   enough where it took no net out and moved none aside, and where it was kept and found no way of its own
   for anything still open: cynthion had runs four and five, 7 s each, for nothing, and no step after them
   that needs two fills.
4. *The first step that takes needless vias out, whatever the time* (the adapter), where a fill is short:
   D121's first measurement, under a load of 31, had lumenpnp-mobo with 488 and 471 vias in two orders of four
   where this step had no time. Not measured under such a load again: the machine was quiet, and the limit of
   fourteen threads does not make one.
5. *The run for shorter ways leaves the spoke step its time* (the adapter), where the board has pads short of
   their spokes with routes in a spoke's room when the runs are over.

### D123. guide 0.0.25 adopted: each net routed again where the others are by the negotiation's search, a run of tracks laid round the corners beside it, forty rounds at twice the pitch and no price for a plane in the negotiation; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's and D122's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on
every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. It does not end there in this round
either, and is nearer. This decision says where the two negotiations part, measured round by round and net by
net, what was ported, what it moved, and what is still behind.
`guide = { version = "0.0.25", default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock`
moves. The table is measured with the crate from crates.io; what led to it, with a checkout of guide behind a
`[patch]` that is in no commit, and with prints and switches in both routers that are in neither release.
**Where the two negotiations part** (measured; tinytapeout-demo, one run of each on three threads).
- *Round by round*: the native router has 2007 points shared after its first round, 57 after its ninth, 18 after
  its twelfth and 2 after its twenty-ninth, and ends at its fortieth, which is all it has (`max_iterations` at
  normal effort), with 255 vias and 4686 mm; its vias go from 184 after the first round to 250 after the
  twelfth and stay. guide 0.0.24, at twice the pitch, has 3210, 164, 108 and then 12 to 116 for 165 rounds more,
  and its vias go from 247 to 410 by the ninth round and to 476 by the hundred and thirty-fifth.
- *The first round is already apart, at the same pitch.* With guide's negotiation forced to the native router's
  pitch of 0.2 mm, after one round, in which each net is routed once with next to nothing priced: 244 vias,
  5153 mm and 5429 points shared against 184, 4494 mm and 2007. By net (dumps of both after that round): the
  ground has 124 connections, 27 vias and 318 mm with guide and 32 connections, no via and 32 mm with the native
  router, which takes the pads that the pour on their own layer joins as joined, where guide plans a net with a
  plane on its inner planes alone; the other nets have 216 vias and 4390 mm against 173 and 4076 mm. With no
  price for a track inside another net's plane and none in the room of a spoke, those have 194 and 4260 mm.
  guide's adapter runs with a track at twice its length inside a plane
  (`RouteOptions::plane_cost`, guide's default), which on a board with planes on two of its four layers makes a
  via half as dear beside a way round as it is to the native router.
- *What the rounds route again is not it.* D113 tried every net near a shared point routed again, within the
  share it then had, and dropped it for the rounds it cost; the negotiation is on threads since D118, so it was
  tried again, as the native router has it: every net whose box is near a shared point, routed again whole, but
  a net of 64 connections or more with nothing shared of its own, which keeps its wires away from the points.
  And the nets of a round one at a time, not eight. And both. The vias after the ninth round are 403 to 406 in
  all three for 410 (one run of each): the same.
- *Nor the pitch alone.* At the native router's pitch with the native router's rising price and its choice of
  the nets to route again, no price for a plane or for the room of a spoke, and the ground planned on every
  pour: 184 vias after the first round, as the native router has, with 4735 mm for 4494 and 2966 points shared
  for 2007; 281 vias after the ninth for 248, and 300 after the twentieth for 258, with 5170 mm for 4741 and 159
  points shared for 37. A round takes 0.4 to 0.6 s, as the native router's. So guide's rounds at that pitch
  cost what the native router's do and settle less; what is left between the two after those differences are
  taken away was not found (inferred, not measured: where a route may end at a pad, which the native router
  lets be any cell on its copper and guide the cells beside its middle).
**What was ported** (guide 0.0.25 but the last, which is the adapter's).
1. *A plane of another net costs a track nothing in guide's negotiation*, as in the native router's. The passes
   that route a net at a time, and move others for it, pay for a plane as they did. At 150 million nodes, four
   orders, medians, with the price and without it: tinytapeout-demo 0, 1, 0 and 4 open with 324 vias and 5133 mm
   for none open with 299 and 5071 mm; buspirate5-rev10 322 vias and 3068 mm for 308.5 and 3017; lumenpnp-mobo
   331.5 and 5483 mm for 333 and 5407; cynthion 418 and 3088 mm for 416.5 and 3072; glasgow-revC3 21 open over
   the four orders with 406.5 vias and 3699 mm for 22 with 395 and 3613.
2. *Forty rounds at most at twice the pitch*, the native router's forty, where guide had a hundred, and a
   negotiation that its last round ended is not begun again in another order. D116 wrote that ending the rounds
   after the twelfth, for the passes to have the time, was not tried: tinytapeout-demo has 44 points shared
   after its fortieth round and 16 to 28 after some 150, and as its rounds end 349 to 388 vias for 394 to 458;
   at 150 million nodes over six orders it ends with 305 vias and 5037 mm with forty rounds for 311.5 and
   5412 mm with a hundred. At the first pitch, where the price of a shared point stops at thirty steps (D115),
   the hundred stay: corne-cherry had 11, 2, 3 and 9 open in four orders at 60 s with forty for 4, 0, 0 and 0.
3. *Each net routed again where the others are, by the negotiation's search* (`whole::again`), which D122
   named and did not attempt. The native router's pass for fewer vias routes each net again once its routes are
   legal, with a via at forty steps; guide's cleanup did the same by the searches that route a net among fixed
   copper, 12.5 s for 76 vias where the negotiation's own search had 0.4 s for 78 as its rounds ended. That
   search knew only the routes it made itself, on its own points. Now a net claims on the grid what its copper
   keeps other nets' away from wherever it lies; copper that is off the grid claims as much more as a track on
   the grid may pass nearer than its points say, between two of them (the native router's `delta`); a net gives
   up its claims while it is routed where nothing is claimed; and what the search finds is kept only if guide's
   exact check allows every track and via of it among the others' copper as it is. The first time through the
   nets is for fewer vias alone, at what cleanup lets a via less cost in track, and the times after for a way
   as short with as many as well. No layer has a direction of its own in it: with the directions that the
   rounds have, buspirate-rs232 kept 7, 6, 6 and 5 vias in four orders where cleanup alone leaves 5, 5, 5 and 4.
   On the negotiation's grid at the end of the first run, 0.5 to 4 s a board (tinytapeout-demo: 294 nets looked
   at and 41 kept in 1.5 s, 12 vias and 81 mm less); at the pitch in the run for shorter ways.
4. *The native router's gridless pass* (`router::gridless`), in guide's cleanup of the run for shorter ways
   (`cleanup::round_corners`): each stretch of a run of tracks is laid as the shortest way through the corners
   of what is beside it, by tracks in the eight directions that the exact check allows, if that is shorter. The
   corners are those of the octagon round each corner of a pad, each end of a track and each via or hole of
   another net, whose sides are as far from it as the track's centre has to stay; the native router has them
   from the hulls of what a track passes. 0.1 to 0.2 s and 15 to 36 mm on a board of four layers
   (lumenpnp-mobo 5986 to 5950 mm, buspirate5-rev10 3094 to 3068, cynthion 3415 to 3401, before the track inside
   the pads is left out).
   tinytapeout-demo at 150 million nodes over six orders, medians, with 1 and 2 in all: 315 vias and 5200 mm
   with this pass alone, 308.5 and 5102 mm with 3 alone, 305 and 5037 mm with both; and 333 and 5202 mm with
   neither, a plane at its price and a hundred rounds, which is 0.0.24.
5. *A pass on the finer lattice that took no net out is the last* (guide 0.0.25), and *no run that moves
   routes after a first run that moved none and found no way* (the adapter, `first_said_all`). D122 ended the
   runs that move routes after one that ended on its own having taken no net out and moved none aside, with
   every open net one whose own search found no way; the first run says the same where it ends so, and the run
   that moves routes searches the same board for the same ways. sweep-v2.2, whose three open connections
   neither router makes, had two passes on the finer lattice for them in its first run, 13 s and 6 s, and a
   run that moves routes of 17 s after it: it has the first of the two passes, and the run for shorter ways,
   which it never had the time for, in place of the other.

### D124. guide 0.0.27 adopted: a net that has no way on the board told once, the time of the step for the spokes kept from the first run on, each net routed again before the fills are joined again; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's, D122's and D123's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every
measure on every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. It does not end there in this
round either. This decision takes D123's two regressions first, cynthion's pads short of their spokes and
glasgow-revD1's track; the first is mended and the second is not. It says what was found, what was changed in
guide and in the adapter, what it moved, and what is still behind.
`guide = { version = "0.0.27", default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock`
moves. Two releases: 0.0.26 has the changes below, and 0.0.27 takes one of them back for runs with a budget of
nodes, where 0.0.26 was worse than 0.0.25 and was released before that was measured (below, "Budgets of nodes").
The table at 60 s is measured with 0.0.27 from crates.io behind this branch's adapter, and was measured with
0.0.26 the same way an hour before: a run with a deadline and no budget of nodes is the same code in both, and the
two measurements say how far the same code moves from one hour to the next. What led to it was measured with a
checkout of guide behind a `[patch]` that is in no commit, and with prints in both that are in neither release.
**What was found** (measured; one run of each on three threads unless said).
- *cynthion's eight nets at its net ties cost a search of the whole board in every pass.* Each has a pad that no
  track leaves at the board's clearance (D117; the native router says "no legal way out of R59.2 for a 0.127mm
  track: pad R59.1"). In guide's first run, 0.0.25: the first pass on the finer lattice 12.5 s and the second
  9.3 s, of which 9.5 s and 9.2 s are one net each time, 6523250 nodes: a search across other nets' routes from
  the pad that routes shut in, which goes over the board before it says that the pad at the tie is not to be
  reached. The seven others end after 2260 nodes. The search that tells a net apart on the board with no route
  (D110) said nothing of any of them: it keeps what it reaches and goes on from the other pad with an eighth of
  its nodes, 500257 here, runs out, and a search that runs out says nothing. So the first run ended at its
  deadline, 42 s, in two orders of four, and the step for the spokes had no time (D123).
- *Telling the needless vias took 2.2 s and 1.9 s on cynthion* (`pcb::needless`, `needless_between`), of which
  1.7 s and 1.5 s for the ground: 597 tracks and vias against 184 pieces of fill. Not the measuring: each piece
  was cut into parts of few edges the first time a point was asked of it, 0.1 to 0.5 s for a piece of a plane.
- *glasgow-revC3's first run had 0.35 s for each net routed again* (D123's item 3), 89 nets of 369: cleanup has
  8 % of what the negotiation leaves, and the joining of what the routes cut off their fills came first.
  glasgow-revD1 has 0.8 s for all of cleanup after a negotiation of 30 s, less than asking the grid of its board
  takes.
- *glasgow-revD1's track is in the nets with as many vias and more.* By net, run 1 of each router in D123's table,
  the 503 nets both complete: 7373 mm for the native router and 7973 mm for guide. The 365 nets with as many vias
  in both have 3064 mm and 3310 mm (+8 %), the 74 where guide has more vias 1736 mm and 2106 mm (+21 %), the 62
  where it has fewer 2557 mm and 2540 mm. At 120 s the first run's cleanup has the time, and the board ends with
  10424 mm and 1130 vias for 10777 mm and 1202 at 60 s, with 10 connections open for 8.
- *corne-cherry's negotiation is 151 rounds in 25 s*: 5389 points shared after the first, 100 after the thirtieth,
  36 to 60 from the sixty-first to the seventy-third, 130 again at the seventy-fourth, and one from the hundred
  and thirty-eighth on, which the rounds do not end. Not acted on.
**What was changed in guide** (0.0.26; its `docs/benchmarks.md` has the measurements).
1. *A net that has no way on the board is told once.* The search with no route on the board is, for a net of two
   pads, the search for the net whole: it says that the net has a way, that it has none, or that it ran out. A
   search across every route of the board, with no net locked, on the finest lattice of the run, that finds no way
   for such a net has said so for the run. And a search that may cross routes has 200000 nodes once it leaves its
   window, then a look as long from its other end, before it has all that it may expand. Such a net has no more
   turns, in no pass and no chain; guide tells it (`Routed::apart`), and its open connection says what shuts the
   pad in where the board's own does (`Cause::Enclosed`, whichever end it is), where `Cause::Apart` alone had
   cadlab say "the board keeps U1.14 apart from R59.2". cynthion's first run: the first pass on the finer lattice
   2.5 s, the second with nothing to do, the net of 9.5 s 0.24 s, the run over at 17 to 21 s in the four orders
   for 20 to 42 s.
2. *Each net routed again where the others are before the fills are joined again*, with half of cleanup's time and
   not with less than a second; the stubs to the fills are then for the routes as they stay. glasgow-revC3 over
   four orders at 60 s: 11, 6, 9 and 8 open with 3589, 3729, 3668 and 3586 mm for 12, 6, 10 and 8 with 3676, 3727,
   3729 and 3635 mm. Not in a run with a budget of nodes (0.0.27, below).
3. *A piece of fill answers its first 4096 points by its edges*, and is cut into parts when it has been asked
   more: the two questions on cynthion 0.34 s and 0.28 s. At 40 million nodes cynthion, glasgow-revC3 and
   tinytapeout-demo have the same connections, vias and track to the tenth of a millimetre with it as without.
**What was changed in the adapter.**
1. *The time of the step for the spokes is kept from the first run on.* D122 kept it from the run for shorter
   ways. Where the board as the first run leaves it has pads short of their spokes with routes in a spoke's room,
   the runs on the filled board and the runs that move routes end in time for the step too, and the step that
   takes out the tracks between pads that a pour joins waits for it where the time is not there for both, and is
   made after it. Thermal relief is required (D120): a pad with its spokes comes before one connection more and
   before a shorter board.
2. *No run in less than twice what the first needed after it*: glasgow-revD1 takes 2 s to verify, and a run of ten
   nets on it had 3.5 s before its first search and 2 s to its deadline.
3. *The nets that guide tells apart* (`Routed::apart`) are left out of the later runs, as those with
   `Cause::Apart` were.

### D125. guide 0.0.29 adopted: in a rule area with a clearance of its own, the nets of a row of pads no wider than its pitch has room for two of, on a lattice of their pitch; the first round of both routers joined connection by connection; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's to D124's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on
every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. It does not end there in this round
either, and is nearer on tinytapeout-demo. This decision has what D123 and D124 named and did not do: the first
round of both routers looked at connection by connection, the differences counted by their kind, the largest
ported into guide and measured. `guide = { version = "0.0.29", default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`;
nothing else in `Cargo.lock` moves, and the adapter is as D124 left it. Two releases: 0.0.28 has the port for
every row of pads, and 0.0.29 has it for the rows in a rule area alone, where 0.0.28 cost corne-cherry
connections at 60 s (below, "0.0.28 and corne-cherry"). The tables at 60 s are measured with 0.0.29 from
crates.io; what led to them, with a checkout of guide behind a `[patch]` that is in no commit, and with prints
and switches in both routers that are in neither release.

print each connection of their first round, in which every net is routed once with next to nothing priced: its
net, the two pads, the layers, the vias and the length. Joined by net and pair of pads. tinytapeout-demo, with
guide's negotiation forced to the native router's pitch of 0.2 mm, as D123 had it: 458 connections, 240 vias,
5055 mm and 3514 points shared for guide; 366 connections, 184 vias, 4494 mm and 2007 points shared for the native
router.

By cause, each measured by a switch in guide that takes it away, in the first round at that pitch:
- *The planning of a net with a plane* (16 vias and 350 mm of the 56 and 561): the ground has 124 connections, 27
  vias and 324 mm with guide and 32 connections, no via and 32 mm with the native router, which takes the pads
  that the pour of their own layer joins as joined (`geo::islands` with the fills) and lets a connection end on
  any cell of a fill within 4 mm of its end (`Engine::pour_targets`), no via needed. +3V3, 68 connections in both,
  has no via and 412 mm with guide, whose via for a net with a plane costs 40 steps at this pitch (D122), and 11
  vias and 355 mm with the native router. Planned on every pour, as D123 tried: 108 connections for 108, 15 vias
  for 11, 465 mm for 419.
- *The room of a spoke*, which costs a track in guide's rounds and nothing in the native router's (17 vias): the
  connections of the same pair with more vias with guide are 27 with 45 for 11 without that price, where they
  are 37 with 66 for 15.
- *The order of the nets*, strides through them for guide and the shortest first for the native router (8 vias):
  32 connections with 55 for 12.
- *The decomposition*, a spanning tree by the distance along the axes for guide and as the crow flies for the
  native router, both grown from the first terminal: 8 nets of 137 with other pairs, 7 vias and 35 mm.
- *Where a route ends at a pad*, which D123 inferred: at the pad's middle for guide, by a track from the grid's
  cell to it, and on the first cell that is on the pad's copper for the native router (`Engine::access`, at no
  cost). The 84 connections of the same pair with no via are 78 mm longer with guide, of which 67 mm are those
  tracks; the native router's routes end 116 mm short of the middles in all. It is track inside the pads, which
  the measure of the track outside them leaves out.
- *The price of a layer change and of a direction* are the same in both (ten steps a via, 1.8 a step across a
  layer's direction, 0.4 and 1.5 a bend, the same estimate of what is left), and so are the claims of a track
  and of a via on the grid. Nothing was found there.
- With all of the above taken away: 194 vias, 4746 mm and 2765 points shared against 184, 4494 mm and 2007, and
  the connections with more vias with guide less those with fewer are four vias. And twelve rounds later 297
  vias, 5076 mm and 49 points shared against 250, 4663 mm and 18.
- *The widths of the nets*, which no switch had: found a connection at a time in what was left. `uio3` from pin
  4 of J15 to pin 1 of J9 is 11.4 mm with guide, round the header, and 6.7 mm with the native router, between the
  two rows of pins: a track of 0.22 mm there is 0.245 mm from a pin of the ground, whose class asks 0.25 mm,
  and the native router routes the net at 0.185 mm. It routes 100 of the board's 137 nets at 0.185 mm for their
  class's 0.22 mm, 22 at 0.235 mm for 0.25 mm and 9 at 0.16 mm; guide 0.0.27 routed 95 of them at 0.22 mm. Both
  make a net narrower for a row of pads of fine pitch, each by its own rule: the native router by the pitch of
  two pads less the net's clearance and what the grid's points miss between two tracks (`fanout::necks`, D39),
  guide by the widest at which two tracks out of two pads side by side clear each other by the clearance of the
  rule area that both are in, which in the courtyard of this board's QFN of 80 pads is 0.16 mm for the board's
  0.2 mm. So 80 tracks of 0.22 mm left that courtyard 0.18 mm apart and had to part at its edge, and every
  passage a track of 0.185 mm has was shut to them.

**Not attempted, or begun and left, and why the parity is not there.** By what it would take:
1. *The planning of a net with a plane* (the first round's largest difference on three boards of four:

   none, tinytapeout-demo's 124 and 27 for 32 and none). guide plans such a net on its inner planes alone and
   takes each pad off them to them; the native router takes what the pours of the outer layers join as joined
   and negotiates again, the other nets making room, for the pads that its routes cut off them. Planned so in
   guide, with the pads cut off told as its rounds end, the boards end worse (above): the pads cut off are
   joined again among routes that the rounds no longer move. What it would take is the native router's order,
   the rounds, then the routes made legal, then the pours filled and the nets cut planned again, then rounds
   again; guide's rounds tell the pads cut off before its routes are legal.

   was found: it is there after guide's first round, on a grid of twice the native router's pitch (10347 mm for

### D126. guide 0.0.30 adopted: a pad's last spoke kept as copper in the runs that move routes that are otherwise final, the step for the spokes kept by the pads with no spoke first, a net routed again kept only if every track of it is free; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's to D125's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on
every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. It does not end there in this round
either, and is no nearer by the count of the cells. What this round has is the first thing asked of it, a pad
left with no spoke by 0.0.29, which thermal relief being required (D120) put before the rest, and a fault found
on the way to it, routes of guide's own that crossed another net's track. Of the four things asked after it,
none is done: below, "Not attempted", says of each what was looked at and what was measured.
`guide = { version = "0.0.30", default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock`
moves.
**How the pad with no spoke was made** (measured: the necks of every pad in a pour counted after each run of
the adapter, a print that is in no commit). J14.5 of tinytapeout-demo is a pin of the ground in a row of pins
2.54 mm apart, with room for two spokes, across the row; D125 had it with none in one order of sixteen at 60 s.
It is made again at 60 s in the fourth order, and there the pad has its two necks after the first run and after
the runs that move routes, and none after the run for shorter ways (D116), in which guide has every route back
to look for a shorter way for each, and lays a track of `ui_in1` along the row on one side of the pin and one of
`ui_in0` on the other. Once guide's fault below is mended the same pad has none at 150 million nodes in the same
order, before the step for the spokes is begun. The
room of a spoke has a price there as in any run (`spoke_cost`, D110), thirty-three times a track's length for a
pad with none to spare, and the two tracks are shorter by more. In D125's run the second of the two is, by the
numbers of its tracks, of the last run that made any (inferred from that run's log, not made again): the step
for the spokes itself (D121), which moved routes out of the rooms of three other pads and was kept. It counted
the pads short of two spokes, seven before and five after, and a pad that goes from one neck to none is one pad
short before and after. The other pad of D125, U6.69 of +3V3 at the QFN, is no relief at all: its
footprint leaves room for no spoke, it reads as a pad with no neck when its connection is open, and in the two
runs that had it so, one of each release, it is one of eleven connections open, shut in by the tracks of the
pins beside it.
**What was changed.**
1. *guide 0.0.30, `RouteOptions::kept_spokes`: a pad's last spoke is a wall.* Of the spokes that the fill makes
   for a pad on a layer (those the adapter gives, D112), the ones with nothing of another net in their room are
   free; the board's own copper takes a room for good, and the directions that the fill falls back to count
   for a pad that the board leaves none of the first. When a route placed in guide's world leaves a pad no more
   free rooms than it keeps, each of those is in the world as copper of the pad's net, which the spoke will be:
   every search and every step of its cleanup keeps the clearance from it, as from any copper, and a route
   taken out of another room takes the wall down. From when guide routes a net at a time: the routes it is
   given are taken as they are, and a room that a route is lifted from is walled only once something is placed
   again, so that a route laid back where it was has its way back. The adapter sets it to one in the run for
   shorter ways and in the step for the spokes (`KEPT_SPOKES`), the two runs that move routes that are
   otherwise final, and in no run that routes (below, "Tried and not kept").
2. *A shorter way that leaves a pad that had a neck with none is not kept*: the nets with new copper at that
   pad have their old routes back, as those at a connection that the run opened have (D116), and the rest is
   verified again.
3. *The step for the spokes is kept by how far the board is from its relief* (`relief_score`): the pads with
   no neck that are to have one, then the pads short of their spokes, then the spokes those lack in all, and
   never with a pad that had a neck left with none. It asks for as many rooms for a pad as the pad lacks
   spokes, where it asked for one; and what the direction named, a room at a time with what is gained kept: a
   try that is kept is the board, and the rooms it has then are tried again; a try in which every net came
   back whole and the pads are no better off is made again with half of the rooms, those of the pads with no
   neck first, down to one; six tries at most, each begun with the time of its run, its fills and its counts.
4. *guide 0.0.30, a net routed again is kept only if every track of it is free.* guide 0.0.25's pass that routes
   each net again where the others are (D123) asked whether the new route is free by counting the tracks that
   `NetCopper::free_in` keeps of it against those it has. `free_in` cuts a track where something is in its way
   and keeps the free steps on either side, and joins what is in line: a track cut in two beside two joined
   into one is as many as before. tinytapeout-demo, the eighth order at 150 million nodes: a track of `ui_in7`,
   3.4 mm straight to its pad of the QFN across a track of the ground and one of +3V3, in guide's own result.
   The adapter's check then takes out every piece of copper that touches such a track (D61), pieces of the
   ground and of +3V3 among them, and the runs after the first join them up again: 120, 107 and 323 tracks and
   vias in three of eight orders at 150 million nodes, 62 and 23 in two of eight at 60 s; D125's order with
   eleven connections open has 23 items taken out and four of the eleven told as `broke a rule and was taken
   out`. Every track and via is asked of the world now, and the check takes nothing out in any order measured.

with three threads for its negotiation; and four more of each on tinytapeout-demo (seeds 5 to 8). *The machine

**Not attempted, or looked at and left, and why the parity is not there.**
1. *The planning of a net with a plane on the pours of the outer layers, in the native router's order* (the
   direction's second item, and D125's largest difference). Read again, guide's negotiation has that order but
   for one step: when its rounds end with nothing shared, or twelve after their best, it has cadlab's fill
   around the routes as they are (`RunControl::refill`, D114), plans the nets again with the pads that the
   fill no longer joins, and goes on with its rounds, three times at most (guide 0.0.19). What the native
   router does that it does not is make the routes legal before the fill. Planned on every pour that way was
   measured twice (D123, D125) and lost; it was not built a third time, with the routes made legal first, in
   this round. buspirate5-rev10's +VUSB, which the direction asked the source of: 43 vias for the native
   router's 19 in a run of each on one thread (the native router's cut by a budget of nodes with 14
   connections open), of 316 for 314 on the board. They are the stubs of guide's first
   run to the fills it plans on (166 stub vias after the first run, of which the fill of the routed board
   makes 66 needless), and its nets with pours have 102 vias and 518 mm of track where the native router's
   have 86 and 662 mm: a via to the pour for a track between two pads. D125 measured that the price of a via
   in those stubs moves three vias of the board.
2. *glasgow-revD1's and glasgow-revC3's track* (+19 % and +6 %; +10 % and +1 % on the nets both complete):
   not begun. Of the direction's third item, the step for the spokes goes on from each try that it keeps
   (above); the time it leaves is not given back to routing, and one try is still a run, a verification and a
   fill.
3. *corne-cherry's time* (35 to 56 s against 19 to 32 s): not begun. Its first run goes to its share of the
   minute in three orders of four with one to five connections open, and its later runs close one to four of
   them; the round of its negotiation was not profiled beside the native router's.
4. *buspirate-flash-sop's via* (5 against 4; 6 against 4 in the first order): looked at by net. The native
   router's routes leave the pour of GND_CHIP in one piece, guide's in two, joined by a route of the net with
   two vias; every other net has the vias it has with the native router, and less track in all (440 mm against
   461). Moving the track that cuts the pour was not attempted.
5. *buspirate-rs232's track* (297 mm against 281, with five vias against ten): looked at by net, in the first
   order (293.8 mm against 280.9). Three nets make 7.1 mm of the 12.9: UART0RX 19.8 mm with no via for 16.5 mm with one, UART1RX 20.5 mm for 17.8 mm, DCE_RXD
   13.2 mm for 12.1 mm; with the native router's choice on those three the board would have eight vias and
   286.7 mm, 2.1 % over. The rest is in connections of 2 to 5 mm between a part and the capacitor beside it,
   0.2 to 0.4 mm each, and in four nets of 16 to 18 mm, 0.2 to 0.7 mm each. A cheaper via was not tried: it
   is the price that keeps the vias of the boards whose vias are worse.
**Default: unchanged.** `router: guide` stays the second opinion and the native router stays the default.
*Not measured:* the generated boards; more than four runs of either router, but tinytapeout-demo's eight;
freerouting beside the two; KiCad's DRC on a board guide routed; cadlab's oracles locally; cadlab's whole test
suite, which is run at the merge; the count of the step for the spokes by the pads with no neck, which takes in
the pads that are not soldered where `thermal::census` leaves them out (buspirate5-rev10: two such pads with no
neck that the step does not mend, and none soldered).

### D127. guide 0.0.31 adopted: a pour left whole and a run ended on its pad in the run for shorter ways, the fills told as clear of the board they were made around, a track ended at the first copper of its pad; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's to D126's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on
every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. This round had the items that several
rounds left: buspirate-flash-sop's via, buspirate-rs232's track, and the time of corne-cherry, tinytapeout-demo
and buspirate5-rev10 (another round, in parallel, has the planning of a net with a plane on outer pours and the
glasgows' track, and nothing of those is here). The first two are done; of the time, what makes nothing was
found and taken out, and the rest is said below with what it is spent on. It does not end at parity.
`guide = { version = "0.0.31", default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock`
moves.
**What was changed.**
1. *guide 0.0.31, a pour left whole (`pcb::uncut`, `Stats::uncut`).* buspirate-flash-sop's fifth via is beside
   C1.2, a pad of GND_CHIP in the pour of the top layer: the tracks of other nets and the pins of J3 between
   which they pass close a ring round it, and a via takes the pad to the pour on the other side (read from
   the tracks of both results). The native router has no rule for it: its tracks happen to leave a way
   between two pins. In its run for shorter ways
   guide now looks at each stub with a via that joins a pad to a pour on the pad's own layer: its cells
   (`pcb::pours`) say whose routes are round the pad's piece of the pour, and where the fill would join the
   pad to its largest piece without the routes of one, two or three of those nets; that way is kept free, as
   copper of the pour's net as wide as the fill needs, the nets are routed again round it at the price of a
   via that the search for fewer vias has, and pulled tight with the way still kept. If they then have no
   more vias than they had, are no longer by more than the stub and 5 mm, and no pad of any pour is cut off
   that was not, the stub goes; if not, everything is as it was. On buspirate-flash-sop VCC_CHIP goes another
   way in three orders of four, 68.4 mm for 66.3, and the via is gone; in the fourth nothing is kept (the one
   way that the fill has costs the net in it two vias for the one). Two things had to be found for it (measured,
   by a map of the cells printed for one pad): the fill that the adapter gives guide is cadlab's fill around
   the routes, so the cells have no fill where a route is, whichever nets are taken as not there, and a cell
   is given back where guide's world has room for copper of the pour's least width with those nets gone
   alone; and the nets routed again went back to the straight line when they were pulled tight after the
   way was given up.
2. *guide 0.0.31, a run's end at a pad (`cleanup::aim_at_pads`).* D125 measured that guide routes to a pad's
   centre and the native router to the first cell of its grid on the pad. A run that comes to a pad beside
   its line (buspirate-rs232: a capacitor's pad 0.25 mm off the line of the driver's pin, twenty times) stepped
   aside for the centre before it was at the pad. In the run for shorter ways each run's end at a pad is
   aimed at a point of the pad's box on one of the eight directions from its centre, half a track's width
   from the box's edge at least, and goes on from there to the centre; of the ways that guide's world allows,
   the one with the least outside the pads of the net, if that is less than the run has.
3. *guide 0.0.31, a via at 2 mm in a run that is searched for again* (`SHORTER_VIA`, 3 mm before). Three nets
   of buspirate-rs232 go between two pins of a driver and round to their own pin from behind, 2.7 to 3.3 mm
   longer than the native router's way with a via; at 3 mm each cost as much with the via as without.
4. *guide 0.0.31, `Zones::fills_clear_of`, and the adapter says it.* The fills that the adapter gives are
   cadlab's own, of the board that it gives with them. guide measured each fill against every pad, track and
   hole near it in every call, to cut it where a route goes through it, and before it measures a fill of many
   edges it makes the parts that it is measured by: 3.6 s of the 4.3 s that the fills took over the six calls
   of a run of buspirate5-rev10 (measured by a clock on each stage, in no release). The adapter now says what
   the fills were made around, the tracks and vias that it hands back to be moved among them, and guide
   measures them against what its run adds alone, with no parts for a fill that has nothing to measure.
5. *The adapter: a track ends at the first copper of its pad* (`pad_ends`). D118 moved an end back along its
   track only for as long as the whole of its round end stayed inside the pad, so that the copper of the board
   was the same shape. A track that runs along a pad beside its middle line, on the pad for its middle and off
   it for a part of its width, was left as long as it was: with its runs aimed as above, buspirate-rs232 had
   13.4 mm of track inside its pads, where the native router has 9.3 mm, and has 8.9 mm. An end is now moved
   back to half the track's width before where the track's middle leaves the pad, as a track of the native router
   that ends on the first cell of the pad is.
   What is cut is copper of the pad's net on the pad or within half a track's width of it.
6. *The adapter: a run that moves routes, ends on its own and leaves more connections open than it was given
   is the last.* corne-cherry, two orders of four: a pad of a ground cut off its pour after the first run, a
   run that moved routes for it and came back with 7 and with 78 connections open, not kept, and a second in
   another order of the nets with as many, 8 to 13 s each.

### D128. guide 0.0.32 adopted: the native router's order for the pours built in guide, the routes made legal before the fill, and a net with a plane planned on its outer pours; measured stage by stage, neither is a gain, both left off; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's to D126's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on
every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. This round had one item, the largest
difference that D125 measured in the first round of the two routers: the native router takes the pads that a
pour of an outer layer joins as joined, and guide plans a net with a plane on its inner planes alone. Planned on
every pour guide lost twice (D123, D125), and D126 read the cause as the order: guide tells the pads cut off on
routes that are not yet legal. **The order was built, and the planning with it, and measured: it is not the
cause. Planned on outer pours with the native router's order guide still ends worse than 0.0.30, and the order
alone gains nothing. Both are options of guide that are off, and the adapter leaves them off; cadlab's results
with guide are those of the release before.** `guide = { version = "0.0.32", default-features = false, features
= ["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock` moves. (D127 is the other change of this round, made beside this
one.)
**What was built** (guide 0.0.32, read from `router::mod`'s `pour_round`, `pour_truth` and `replan_pours` and
written again for guide's negotiation).
1. *`RouteOptions::legal_pours`.* When the rounds end, at nothing shared, at twelve with none better or at their
   most, the routes go back to the best round and are made legal: what is shared is taken out, the net with the
   most first, and routed again where nothing is claimed (`whole::legalise`, which was the end of the
   negotiation and is now a step of it). cadlab's fill around those routes is asked for (`RunControl::refill`),
   and the connections open on that board are counted, the pads cut off their fills among them
   (`whole::open_on_fills`), as the native router counts its ratsnest on `pour_truth`. The nets whose pads the
   fill no longer joins are planned again and the rounds go on for them, the other nets making room. When
   those rounds end the routes are made legal and the pours filled again, and with more connections open than
   on the legal board that the nets were planned again from, the routes go back to that board
   (`Stats::pours_back`; the native router's `PourSnapshot`). Three times at most.
2. *One step is not the native router's.* The rounds go on from the routes of the best round as they were, and
   not from the legal ones. Made as the native router has it, a net that was taken out and found no way where
   nothing is claimed has no round again, and is left to guide's passes, which take other nets out for it:
   tinytapeout-demo, the default order at 150 million nodes, 16 connections apart as the passes begin for 10,
   202 rip-ups in them for 44, 439 vias after them for 365, and 291 at the end for 270 (measured, below).
3. *`RouteOptions::outer_pours`.* A net with a plane is planned as one with none is: on every fill of its
   zones, so that the pads a pour of an outer layer joins are one terminal. With it, a negotiation that is
   still at its first rounds at 0.73 of its share looks once at what its routes cut off, by guide's cells, and
   ends those rounds for the pours if that is a piece of fill for every hundred connections: the native
   router's look at 0.55 of its budget, where its rounds end at 0.75.

### D129. guide 0.0.33 adopted: the connections that its negotiation leaves open negotiated for on the grid of the pitch, built and measured stage by stage: it halves what the passes take out and the board ends as it did, left off; the round's table on a quiet machine, the glasgows' track by net, corne-cherry's connections and time; the default unchanged (2026-11-23)
The direction is D121's to D128's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on
every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. This round had D128's three open
items in its order: the passes after a negotiation that ended well, the track of the two glasgows, and
corne-cherry. **The first was built and measured stage by stage: the connections that guide's negotiation
leaves open are negotiated for on the grid of the pitch before the passes, which halves what the passes are
given and the nets they take out, and the board ends as it did. It is an option of guide that is off, and the
adapter leaves it off; cadlab's results with guide are those of the release before. The other two were looked
at and measured, and nothing of them is changed: what was found is below.** `guide = { version = "0.0.33",
default-features = false, features = ["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock` moves.

**What was built** (guide 0.0.33, `RouteOptions::whole_finer`; read from `router::mod`'s rip-up and retry after
its rounds, which takes the nets in a failing net's way out together and keeps the routes only with fewer
connections failing, and written for guide's negotiation).
1. When guide's rounds at twice the pitch end, what is still shared is taken out and routed again where
   nothing is claimed, and each net is routed once more for fewer vias, as before. A net that was taken out
   and found no way has a connection open on the grid.
2. The nets are then put as they are on a grid with a cell between every two of theirs, the same copper
   (`whole::refined`), and there are rounds on it (`whole::finer_rounds`): the nets with a connection open are
   routed across the others at eight steps a claimed point; the nets whose claims they are in are routed again
   in the next round, their wires that are in no one's way kept, at a price that rises by 1.6 a round. Sixteen
   rounds at most, five since the best, in a tenth of the time and of the nodes that the run has left.
3. The routes go back to the round with the fewest points shared, what is still shared there is taken out as
   in step 1, and the routes of that grid are the negotiation's only if fewer connections are open on it than
   before the rounds (`Stats::whole_finer`): the native router's rule for its retries.

   20 to 31 s with two to four open; guide's orders with none open end in 34 to 56 s. Its rounds from the
   thirty-first on (D124, D125, D127) were not changed again.
4. *The node cost of guide's rounds at the first pitch* (tinytapeout-demo: 95 to 143 million nodes in a share
   of 30 s on three threads without ending, for the native router's 38 rounds): not looked at.
**Default: unchanged.** `router: guide` stays the second opinion and the native router stays the default.
*Not measured:* more than one period at 60 s for the option; `whole_finer` on the two-layer boards at 60 s,
where the rounds are at the first pitch and it does nothing; the generated boards; freerouting; KiCad's DRC on
a board guide routed; cadlab's oracles locally; cadlab's whole test suite, which is run at the merge.

### D130. guide 0.0.34 adopted: the native router's negotiation itself in guide, as a first stage that a host can ask for, which ends its rounds as the native router does, round for round on two boards; with guide's passes after it a board has fewer vias and less track and more connections open, and it is left off; the default unchanged (2026-11-24)
The direction is D121's to D129's: guide is to end equal to or better than the native router on every measure on
every board, by taking from the native router what it still does better. Six rounds took a piece at a time
(the set routed again, a net at a time, the price of a plane, the order, the tree, where a route ends at a pad,
the widths, the plan on the outer pours, the routes made legal first), each explained a part, and guide's
negotiation still did not end where the native router's does. **So this round the native router's negotiation
is in guide as it is, whole: `RouteOptions::rounds`, `Rounds::Native`, guide 0.0.34. It ends its rounds as the
native router ends them: the same nets, shared points, vias and track in every round on corne-cherry and
buspirate5-rev10, and within a few vias in a hundred on tinytapeout-demo and glasgow-revD1. With guide's
passes after it, of the three boards whose rounds end in their share, tinytapeout-demo and buspirate5-rev10
have some 5 % fewer vias and 6 % less track than with guide's own rounds, the first with four to seven
connections open for none or one and the second in 34 to 40 s for 20 to 33 s, and lumenpnp-mobo has 1.5 %
more vias and 3 % more track. The adapter leaves it off ([`ROUNDS`], `router::guide`), and cadlab's results with guide are those of
0.0.33, to the via at a budget of nodes.** `guide = { version = "0.0.34", default-features = false, features =
["pcb"] }`; nothing else in `Cargo.lock` moves.
**What is in guide** (its `pcb::rounds`; `docs/benchmarks.md` there has the tables). `router::{engine, grid,
index, pours, fanout, components, scoped, work}` as they are here, less the gridless search, with the board
made from guide's `Design` in place of the project (`model`), and of `router::mod` what a negotiation is:
- the grid (`make_grid`, `snap_pitch`, `alignment`), the plan of the nets (`plan`, `plan_net`: islands, the
  fills among them, the tree by the crow's distance), the access of the pads (`Engine::access`), the batches,
  the search and its prices, the set routed again each round with the partial rip-up of a net of 64
  connections, the order, the seeded shuffle, forty rounds or twelve with none better, the best round kept;
- the legalisation, the rounds for the pours (`pour_round`, `replan_pours`, `pour_truth` by cadlab's fill
  through guide's `RunControl::refill`, with the look at two thirds of the stage), the rip-up and retry of
  a connection with the nets in its way (`blocking_keys`), and the pass for fewer vias (`minimize_vias`);
- the widths (`fanout::necks`) and the ways out (`fanout::plan`, `crossovers`, `escape`), which guide has in
  place of its own necks and escapes in every run of a board whose first run has these rounds. Both tell a
  row and an array by the pads of one part, which guide's design did not have: `Design::parts`, by pad,
  from this adapter.
Not ported: the gridless searches and their retry, push-and-shove, the re-plan of boxed pads, the finer
grids, the optimiser and the verification, which are after the negotiation and are guide's passes there.
The scoped rules are guide's two: an area's clearance between two pieces of copper that both touch it, and
a clearance of an item's own (`scoped::Scoped::new` from guide's `Rules`); guide has no rule by kind or
containment, which this adapter already passes the stricter way (D96). Each net's route goes to guide's
passes as a tree, as its own negotiation's does, with the places where routes end that are no pad's centre.
